thread:
Tessa Morgan: Final pre-beta review thread for Suggestions view. Last pass items before we sign off: a11y, table density, mobile behavior, and wording ("batching" vs "continuous batching"). Please drop any last-call issues here.

Alicia Perez: a11y: risk chips. Current Medium (amber) on light bg is borderline. I checked in Chrome devtools contrast and it’s ~3.2:1 for text in the chip at 12px. We need AA (4.5:1) since it’s conveying info.

Svetlana Orlov: +1. Our DS chip component supports “strong” variants w/ darker text + border. If we use `Chip tone="warningStrong"` it passes. I can update the token mapping in the spec.

Kenji Nakamura: Drawer: keyboard nav. The drawer has an accordion for “Basis of estimate” + “How to implement”. Right now focus starts at the close button (good) but tab order skips the accordion headers when collapsed (bad). We should make the header a button w/ aria-expanded.

Dylan Brooks: Good catch. In PR-18681 I think we used a div header. Nora can you confirm? If it’s div, we’ll swap to DS Accordion component.

Nora Ahmed: Yep currently a div w/ onClick (oops). I’ll swap to DS Accordion today and make sure it keeps focus + screen reader labels. Also will add ESC-to-close.

Marissa Cole: Terminology: we’ve got a mix of “Batching” and “Continuous batching” across list + drawer. We should pick one for UI labels. My vote: “Batching” as the user-facing label, and explain it’s continuous batching in the “Why this helps” section.

Tessa Morgan: Agree. “Continuous batching” reads like an implementation detail. Let’s do:
- Suggestion type: “Batching”
- In details: “This uses continuous batching under the hood…” (w/ learn more link)

Alicia Perez: +1. Also in the filter dropdown it currently says “Continuous batching” which makes the list feel more technical than caching. I’ll update copy in Figma.

Svetlana Orlov: Table density: in the list page, current row height is 56px w/ two-line description. On smaller laptops it feels very tall + scroll-heavy. DS guidance: default = 48px and truncate secondary line w/ tooltip.

Kenji Nakamura: I’m worried truncation hides the “where it applies” context (route/model/region). Can we keep “Applies to” as a column but compress it (e.g., `route • model • region` chips) and one-line only?

Tessa Morgan: We can do one-line “Applies to” with ellipsis + show full in hover + drawer. For beta we mostly need scanability.

Dylan Brooks: Perf wise, fewer lines per row also helps virtualization. Right now the table reflows a lot.

Nora Ahmed: Implementation idea: keep row height fixed (48px), show suggestion title + risk chip inline, and move “Applies to” into a dedicated column (single line). Savings stays right-aligned.

Alicia Perez: Mobile responsiveness: on narrow widths the table should switch to cards. Currently it just horizontal scrolls and the risk chip gets cut off.

Svetlana Orlov: DS has `ResponsiveTable` pattern: at < 768px it becomes stacked rows (key/value). We can also do cards with DS ListItem. Either is ok but we should decide now.

Marissa Cole: For beta: simplest is stacked rows (key/value) + keep filters accessible. Card view is more design work + QA.

Kenji Nakamura: Drawer on mobile: should be full-screen, not a side panel. If it’s side panel it’s ~40% width and content becomes cramped.

Nora Ahmed: We can make drawer “modal” on mobile breakpoint (full-screen) and keep side drawer on desktop. DS Drawer supports `placement="bottom"` for small screens.

Leila Farouk: QA note: please don’t make hover tooltips the only way to see full text (mobile + keyboard). If we truncate, we need accessible expand or show full content in drawer.

Tessa Morgan: +1. Truncate in table is ok as long as:
- there’s a “View details” affordance (row click) and
- for keyboard users, row is focusable and Enter opens drawer.

Dylan Brooks: On that note: row click vs explicit “Open” button? Row click is nice but a11y can get messy.

Svetlana Orlov: DS recommendation: make the primary cell a link/button (title) rather than entire row clickable. Entire-row click creates weird focus/hover states.

Alicia Perez: I prefer title as link + keep rest static. We can still support clicking whitespace later.

Nora Ahmed: Cool, I’ll implement title as button (opens drawer) and add `aria-label="Open suggestion details"`.

Marissa Cole: Copy: “Estimated savings” label. In some mocks it says “Guaranteed savings” in a tooltip (older variant). Please ensure no “guaranteed” anywhere.

Tessa Morgan: Confirmed. “Estimated savings” only. Also add “Based on your last 7 days” line when we have it; otherwise show “Insufficient data” empty state.

Kenji Nakamura: Risk chip placement: currently risk is after savings, far right. For scanability it should be near the title so it’s seen early.

Alicia Perez: +1. Put Risk under the title (small chip). Savings stays right aligned.

Dylan Brooks: Works. Also helps avoid the chip being offscreen on horizontal scroll.

Leila Farouk: Another a11y nit: the risk chip colors need non-color cue (icon or text). If we already have “Low / Medium / High” text in chip, we’re good.

Svetlana Orlov: Chip includes the text label, so non-color cue is satisfied. We can also add a small icon (triangle/exclamation) but not required.

Tessa Morgan: Action items I’m hearing:
1) Update risk chip tokens to pass AA (Svetlana)
2) Swap drawer accordions to DS Accordion w/ aria-expanded + proper focus order (Nora)
3) Terminology: use “Batching” everywhere; explain continuous batching in details (Alicia/Tessa)
4) Table density to 48px + single-line columns + accessible open via title button (Nora)
5) Mobile: list uses stacked key/value table; drawer becomes full-screen/bottom placement (Nora)

Marissa Cole: +1. Once those land, I’m comfortable signing off for beta.

Dylan Brooks: Same. If we can get these in before the release train, great. If anything slips, prioritizing (1) a11y + (2) terminology.

Nora Ahmed: I’ll take (2)(4)(5) today/tomorrow. Will post PR links in #eng once up.

Svetlana Orlov: I’ll push the chip token update + note to design system consumers. Should be a small change.

Alicia Perez: I’ll update Figma copy + the responsive behavior annotations and share link here.

Tessa Morgan: Thanks all. Marking this as the final design review for beta pending the above tweaks.
